query: Is life imprisonment always for whole life or can it mean fixed years?

gold_references.label: Section 6
gold_references.role: life imprisonment reckoned as twenty years unless otherwise provided

gold_references.label: Section 71
gold_references.role: repeat offender punishment involving remainder of natural life

acceptable_references.label: Section 4
acceptable_references.reason: Lists imprisonment for life as a punishment

wrong_references.label: Section 62
wrong_references.reason: Attempt provision, not the main answer to life imprisonment duration

required_points: Life imprisonment should not be stated as always exactly one fixed duration.
Section 6 says life imprisonment is reckoned as equivalent to twenty years unless otherwise provided.
Some provisions can require imprisonment for the remainder of natural life.
optional_points: The answer may explain that context matters.
forbidden_points: Life imprisonment always means exactly twenty years.
Life imprisonment always means the whole natural life in every case.
Section 62 is the main rule for the meaning of life imprisonment.

notes: Good test for retrieval plus reasoning. Section 62 should not be selected as the final legal basis.
